title: Cocrystal Pharma Insiders Purchase $1.03 Million in Private Placement Priced At-the-Market Under Nasdaq Rules
body_text: Cocrystal Pharma Insiders Purchase $1.03 Million in Private Placement Priced At-the-Market Under Nasdaq Rules October 30, 2025 Download as PDF Investment by Directors and Management demonstrates confidence in the Company Potential for an additional $ 1.8 million upon the exercise in full of warrants BOTHELL, Wash., Oct. 30, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cocrystal Pharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: COCP) (the “Company” or “Cocrystal”) announces the completion of a private placement of units priced at-the-market under Nasdaq rules with 743,024 shares of its common stock at a purchase price of $1.39 per unit for proceeds of $1.03 million and unregistered warrants to purchase up to 1,486,048 shares of common stock at an exercise price of $1.24 per share. The warrants are exercisable upon issuance and will expire in 27 months. The four Investors in the private placement are Cocrystal Directors Phillip Frost, M.D., who co-founded the Company and serves as Chairman and CEO of OPKO Health, Inc., Fred Hassan, who is Chairman of the investment firm Caret Group and Director of the private equity firm Warburg Pincus and Richard Pfenniger, and Cocrystal co-CEO and CFO James Martin. “It’s gratifying to join these distinguished board members, who are respected industry veterans, in a shared our commitment to advancing Cocrystal’s mission of addressing the global need for novel antiviral therapies,” said Mr. Martin. “These investments have strengthened our balance sheet as we approach key milestones in our antiviral clinical programs.” The potential additional proceeds to the Company from the warrants, if fully exercised on a cash basis, will be approximately $1.83 million. No assurance can be given that any of these warrants will be exercised. The Company intends to use the net proceeds from this offering to support its clinical development programs, for working capital and general corporate purposes. The unregistered securities described above were offered in a private placement under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and Regulation D promulgated thereunder and have not been registered under the Securities Act, or applicable state securities laws. Accordingly, the unregistered shares and shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of the warrants may not be offered or sold in the United States except pursuant to an effective registration statement or an applicable exemption from the registration requirements of the Securities Act and such applicable state securities laws. This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any of the securities described herein, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or other jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to the registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or other jurisdiction. About Cocrystal Pharma, Inc. Cocrystal Pharma, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company that addresses significant unmet needs by developing innovative antiviral treatments for challenging diseases including influenza, viral gastroenteritis, COVID, and hepatitis. Cocrystal employs unique structure-based technologies and Nobel Prize-winning expertise to create viable antiviral drugs. body_text: Introduction: The evolution of healthcare data and the AI imperative Healthcare organizations are drowning in data. Electronic health records, lab results, billing systems, wearable devices, patient monitoring systems. It never stops. Without the right tools to make sense of it all, this mountain of information becomes more burden than asset. AI-powered business intelligence tools are changing that. They turn massive datasets into insights you can actually use to improve patient care and run operations more efficiently. These platforms use machine learning and predictive analytics to spot patient risks before symptoms show up, figure out where to allocate resources, and help clinicians make better decisions when it matters most. The big shift is how AI integrates with the healthcare software you already use, like EHR systems. Instead of just storing patient data, these systems now surface real-time insights that help doctors make better calls. They enable personalized treatment plans, make population health management actually manageable, and help insurance payers figure out which members need attention. The numbers are hard to ignore. Healthcare AI is projected to save the U.S. economy $150 billion annually by 2026. This isn’t some distant promise anymore. Organizations are seeing real returns through fewer readmissions, smarter staffing, and catching diseases earlier. The growing data deluge in healthcare Every patient interaction creates data. Every test generates results. Every claim leaves a record. Hospitals, clinics, and insurers are generating information faster than anyone imagined possible ten years ago. The problem isn’t the volume. It’s not having tools to actually use it. Raw data sitting in disconnected systems doesn’t improve anything. It just creates storage costs and compliance headaches. Healthcare BI tools fix this by pulling data from all over the place into one view. They connect EHRs, billing platforms, lab systems, and imaging databases to paint a complete picture of patient health and how your organization is performing. This matters because you can’t analyze what you can’t see. Predictive analytics takes it further by looking at historical patient data to spot trends and make forecasts. Which patients are likely headed for readmission? Where will demand spike next month? Which populations need targeted help? These questions become answerable when you can process and analyze data at scale. Bridging the gap: What are healthcare AI BI tools? Healthcare AI BI tools let providers switch from reactive to proactive care. Instead of responding to crises after they happen, hospitals can predict and prevent them. High-risk patients get flagged before symptoms appear. Staffing shortages show up before they hurt care quality. Equipment gets maintained before it fails. These tools support data-driven decisions across clinical, financial, and administrative work. Clinicians get insights that shape treatment plans. Operations teams optimize how they use resources. Finance departments improve revenue cycle management. Everyone works from the same accurate, current information. Cloud-based BI solutions have become the go-to deployment model. The reasons are pretty straightforward: scalability and cost-efficiency. Small clinics can access enterprise-grade analytics without massive infrastructure investments. Large health systems can scale up or down based on what they actually need. Integration with EHR systems is non-negotiable for modern healthcare BI platforms. Seamless data aggregation from your existing clinical systems means insights happen in real-time, not after waiting for batch processing. Clinicians see what they need within their normal workflows instead of switching to separate reporting systems. The promise of AI-powered insights for healthcare AI tools in healthcare have moved past the experimental phase. The technology boosts resource efficiency and expands care capabilities in ways manual analysis never could. Risk stratification that used to require extensive manual review now happens automatically. Predictive models that took weeks to build now generate in hours. Azure Health Insights shows what enterprise healthcare AI looks like in practice. The platform offers predictive models for risk assessment, clinical trial optimization, and population health management while staying HIPAA and GDPR compliant. These aren’t theoretical capabilities. Healthcare organizations use them every day to improve outcomes. Arcadia takes a different approach by putting AI-driven insights directly into clinical systems. Instead of making clinicians switch contexts, the insights appear where they’re already working. This cuts friction and makes it way more likely that insights actually influence care decisions. Health Catalyst provides predictive analytics built specifically for population health management. The system spots patterns in patient data that signal emerging health risks across entire populations. This enables targeted interventions before small issues become major problems. The clinical decision-making improvements are real. AI-powered predictive analytics help care teams anticipate challenges and optimize resources proactively. Quality of care improves when clinicians have better information at the right moment. Why AI-powered business intelligence is critical for healthcare today Healthcare operates under unique pressures that make AI-powered BI particularly valuable. Regulatory compliance is strict. Patient safety stakes are high. Margins are thin. Operational complexity is enormous. Traditional analytics approaches buckle under this combination. AI-powered BI tools address these challenges head-on. They identify high-risk patients before symptoms appear, enabling preventive interventions that improve outcomes and cut costs. Real-time dashboards help hospitals predict readmissions and optimize staff across shifts and departments. Compliance with HIPAA and GDPR isn’t optional. Healthcare BI systems need solid data governance features like audit trails, encryption, and granular user access controls. The best platforms make compliance easier, not harder. They automate reporting requirements and flag potential violations before they happen. The integration of AI-powered BI with EHR systems improves data aggregation and supports strategic decision-making. Clinical data combines with financial and administrative information to give leaders complete visibility. This holistic view enables optimization that wouldn’t be possible when each domain operates independently. Cloud-based solutions have gained traction because they offer scalability and cost efficiency that on-premises deployments can’t match. Healthcare organizations get flexible, real-time data insights without massive capital expenditures or dedicated infrastructure teams. Enhancing patient care and improving patient outcomes AI tools improve patient outcomes by using predictive models to stratify patient risk. Early intervention becomes possible when you can identify which patients are likely to get worse before they show obvious symptoms. This shifts care from reactive treatment to proactive management. Advanced analytics capabilities help predict future health outcomes with increasing accuracy. The systems learn from historical data, spot patterns that indicate risk, and flag patients who need extra monitoring or intervention. This happens continuously, not just at scheduled appointments. Integrating AI into clinical workflows provides real-time decision support without disrupting how people already work. Clinicians don’t need to leave their EHR or change their processes. The AI surfaces relevant insights within familiar interfaces, making adoption feel natural. AI tools analyze medical records and clinical notes way faster than humans can. This speed enables earlier disease detection and better-informed treatment planning. Radiologists get immediate alerts about critical findings. Oncologists see treatment recommendations based on the latest genomic data. Primary care physicians get notified about patients who’ve missed important screenings. Health Catalyst pulls data from multiple sources to predict patient risks and optimize resource allocation. This supports value-based care models where outcomes matter more than service volume. Providers can focus limited resources on patients who need them most while maintaining quality across their entire population. Optimizing operational efficiency and resource allocation Healthcare providers face constant pressure to do more with less. AI-powered BI helps by identifying inefficiencies and optimization opportunities that would be invisible in manual analysis. Staffing models improve when you can accurately forecast patient volumes by department and time of day. Supply chain costs drop when you can predict usage patterns and optimize inventory. Cloud-based BI solutions support this optimization through built-in scalability and easy maintenance. Adding new data sources or expanding to new facilities doesn’t require major infrastructure projects. The flexibility lets healthcare organizations adapt quickly as needs change. Real-time analytics and dashboards let managers monitor key performance indicators continuously. When metrics drift outside acceptable ranges, alerts fire immediately. This enables rapid response to emerging issues before they cascade into major problems. Integration with EHR systems makes seamless data aggregation possible, which is essential for operational management. Patient flow, bed utilization, equipment status, and staff availability all connect in unified views. Operations teams see the complete picture instead of isolated snapshots. Advanced BI functionality lets healthcare organizations anticipate challenges proactively. Predictive models forecast seasonal demand spikes, identify potential bottlenecks, and suggest resource reallocation. Care quality improves when resources align with actual needs rather than historical averages. Navigating complex data and regulatory landscapes Healthcare operates in one of the most regulated industries. HIPAA, GDPR, HITECH, and various state privacy laws create complex compliance requirements. Healthcare AI and BI tools help organizations meet these obligations while still extracting value from sensitive patient data. Integration capabilities matter enormously here. BI platforms need to connect with EHRs, billing systems, lab databases, and imaging archives while maintaining security and compliance across all connections. Strong integration reduces the risk of data exposure during transfers and ensures consistent governance policies. Healthcare organizations use BI tools to automate compliance reporting and manage regulatory requirements efficiently. Manual compliance processes are expensive, error-prone, and don’t scale. Automated systems reduce administrative burden while improving accuracy and auditability. Power BI has become a leading platform in healthcare analytics because it offers powerful solutions for both operational and clinical data analysis. The Microsoft ecosystem integration appeals to healthcare organizations already using Office 365 and Teams for collaboration. Real-time analytics enable proactive identification and management of patient risks and operational challenges. Waiting until weekly reports to discover problems means you’re always behind. Continuous monitoring with automated alerting keeps care teams informed and responsive. Key AI-powered capabilities to look for in healthcare BI tools Not all healthcare BI tools are built the same. The specific AI capabilities they offer vary significantly, and those differences matter for real-world performance. The best platforms combine multiple AI technologies to address different analytical challenges. AI-powered analytics help hospitals predict staffing shortages before they happen, detect billing anomalies that signal fraud or errors, and identify high-risk patients before they need critical care. These capabilities operate continuously in the background, monitoring data streams and flagging situations that need human attention. Predictive models help payers with risk stratification and utilization management optimization. Identifying which members are likely to generate high costs enables targeted care management programs that improve outcomes while controlling expenses. This is essential for value-based care models. Healthcare BI tools with deep EHR integration and compliance-focused reporting streamline data aggregation for clinical, financial, and administrative decision-making. The integration reduces duplication, improves data quality, and ensures everyone works from the same source of truth. The integration of AI enhances clinical workflows and decision-making rather than replacing human judgment. Clinicians maintain full control while receiving intelligent assistance that makes their work more efficient and effective. This augmentation approach drives better outcomes without requiring massive workflow changes. Real-time dashboards and interactive visualization let healthcare managers monitor key performance indicators and respond quickly to emerging issues. Static reports that sit in email don’t drive action. Dynamic dashboards that update constantly and send alerts when needed do. Advanced predictive analytics and forecasting Advanced predictive analytics in healthcare leverage AI-driven models to identify patterns in patient data and forecast potential health issues. This forward-looking capability transforms how care teams allocate time and resources. Instead of treating everyone the same, they can focus on patients with the highest risk. Predictive analytics tools use machine learning to anticipate patient deterioration and improve both patient safety and cost efficiency by reducing readmissions. Hospital readmissions within 30 days are expensive, often preventable, and penalized by Medicare. Predictive models that identify at-risk patients enable targeted discharge planning and post-acute follow-up. These analytics help healthcare providers optimize resource allocation by forecasting patient outcomes and anticipating challenges. Emergency department volumes, surgical case loads, and bed demand all follow predictable patterns once you have enough historical data and good models. This predictability enables better planning. The integration of AI-powered predictive analytics significantly enhances clinical decision-making and care quality improvement. Clinicians get recommendations based on evidence from thousands of similar cases rather than relying solely on their own experience. This collective intelligence raises the baseline quality of care. Healthcare organizations should prioritize BI tools with machine learning capabilities that can analyze patient data trends and forecast future health outcomes. The models need regular updating as population characteristics change and new treatments become available. Platforms that automate model retraining save significant data science effort. Natural language processing for unstructured data Natural language processing extracts insights from unstructured medical data like clinical notes, discharge summaries, and research papers. This matters because most healthcare data is unstructured text rather than neat database fields. Leveraging this text dramatically expands what you can analyze. IBM Watson Health uses advanced NLP to interpret unstructured clinical notes and patient records for clinical decision support. The system reads physician notes, identifies key clinical information, and surfaces relevant research or treatment protocols. This happens in real-time as notes are written. NLP technology helps computers understand and analyze human language, which is particularly useful for medical records. Medical terminology is complex, full of abbreviations, and highly contextual. Good NLP systems trained on medical text handle this complexity far better than general-purpose language models. Healthcare AI tools that incorporate NLP improve efficiency by turning unstructured data into actionable insights. A patient might mention concerning symptoms in an intake form that gets overlooked in manual review. NLP systems flag these mentions automatically, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks. Advanced NLP supports personalized treatment options and predictive modeling by interpreting vast datasets. Genomic reports, pathology findings, and radiology impressions all contain information that influences treatment decisions. NLP makes this information computationally accessible for the first time. Machine learning and AutoML for automated insights ThoughtSpot leverages AI-driven insights to automatically identify anomalies, trends, and correlations without requiring users to build complex dashboards. This makes advanced analytics accessible to non-technical healthcare administrators and clinicians who understand their domain but lack data science training. AutoML capabilities within AI-powered analytics tools offer healthcare organizations automated pattern and trend detection that enhances clinical decision-making and optimizes resource allocation. The systems handle algorithm selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model validation automatically. Users specify what they want to predict, and the platform does the technical work. AI-powered insights engines like ThoughtSpot’s SpotIQ enable automatic analysis of vast datasets to derive meaningful analytics without manual intervention. The system monitors data continuously, identifies statistically significant changes, and explains what’s driving those changes in business terms. Platforms like Power BI integrate AI and machine learning to generate predictive insights from healthcare data while remaining budget-friendly. The pricing starts at $10 per user monthly for Pro licenses, making enterprise-grade AI analytics accessible to smaller healthcare organizations. The integration of AI and AutoML is driving increased adoption of cloud-based solutions for their scalability and cost-efficiency. Organizations don’t need large on-premises infrastructure or dedicated data science teams to benefit from machine learning anymore. Computer vision for medical imaging analysis AI-driven healthcare analytics significantly enhance the clarity and speed of medical imaging interpretation. Radiologists reviewing hundreds of scans daily benefit enormously from AI assistance that flags concerning findings and prioritizes urgent cases. This augmentation improves both speed and accuracy. Integration of AI models in medical imaging allows for real-time prioritization and diagnosis of critical conditions like brain hemorrhages and strokes. Minutes matter for these conditions. AI systems that continuously monitor imaging queues and automatically escalate critical cases accelerate intervention and save lives. High-speed radiology diagnostics are made possible by advanced learning models and GPU-accelerated computing. Processing medical images requires substantial computational power. Modern platforms leverage cloud GPUs to deliver results in seconds rather than minutes. AI applications in medical imaging reduce radiologist workload by efficiently flagging urgent cases through continuous scanning. The systems work around the clock without fatigue, ensuring no critical finding sits unreviewed overnight or during shift changes. This constant vigilance improves safety. Adoption of AI in medical imaging has shown substantial reductions in diagnostic errors, particularly in radiology and oncology. Studies show error rates dropping 20-30% when radiologists work with AI assistance compared to unaided interpretation. These accuracy improvements directly impact patient outcomes. Generative AI for enhanced productivity and data exploration Generative AI leverages advanced algorithms to create new content that aids decision-making and automates workflows. In healthcare, this includes drafting clinical summaries, generating patient education materials, and creating documentation that would otherwise require manual writing. Two prevalent models in healthcare generative AI are Large Language Models for human language tasks and Generative Adversarial Networks for creating synthetic data like medical images. LLMs excel at understanding and generating text. GANs excel at creating realistic images that can supplement limited training datasets. This technology streamlines administrative tasks by automating routine communications and document drafting. Patient appointment reminders, prior authorization requests, and referral documentation all follow predictable patterns. Generative AI handles these routine items, freeing staff for work that requires human judgment. Generative AI is particularly useful for clinical summarization, which helps reduce cognitive workload through more efficient chart reviews. Clinicians spend substantial time reading through lengthy medical histories. AI-generated summaries highlight the most relevant information, making reviews faster and more focused. The adoption of generative AI in healthcare improves handling of complex records by surfacing relevant clinical context. When a patient has a 20-year history across multiple providers, finding specific past events is challenging. AI assistants can quickly locate relevant episodes and present them in context. Top healthcare AI BI tools: A comprehensive overview The healthcare BI market includes dozens of vendors offering various combinations of features, pricing models, and deployment options. Understanding which tools excel in specific areas helps organizations make informed choices rather than defaulting to whatever their IT department already uses. Healthcare BI tools provide functionalities like custom KPI tracking, automated alerts, and mobile access for real-time data visualization. These features ensure insights are accessible when and where decisions happen, not just at desks during business hours. Leading healthcare BI tools recommended for their effectiveness include Holistics, Precision BI, Power BI, Tableau, Sisense, Domo, Looker Studio, and ThoughtSpot. Each has particular strengths. Power BI excels at Microsoft ecosystem integration. Tableau leads in visualization capabilities. Sisense offers strong embedded analytics. Integration with EHR systems is crucial for healthcare BI tools. Seamless data aggregation from Epic, Cerner, Meditech, and other clinical systems eliminates manual data transfers and ensures analysis reflects current patient information. Poor EHR integration kills adoption faster than any other factor. Cloud-based BI solutions are gaining market share due to their scalability, ease of maintenance, and cost efficiency. Organizations avoid large capital expenditures for servers and storage while gaining flexibility to scale up or down based on actual usage. The economics favor cloud for most healthcare organizations. Healthcare BI tools support clinical, financial, and administrative decisions aimed at enhancing patient outcomes and operational efficiency through data-driven insights. The best platforms serve multiple stakeholder groups from a single data foundation, ensuring everyone works from consistent information. Leading general BI platforms with strong healthcare AI integration Power BI is known for budget-friendly healthcare reporting and seamless integration with the Microsoft ecosystem. Pricing starts at $10 per user per month for Pro licenses, making it accessible to organizations of all sizes. The Azure integration provides enterprise-grade security and compliance features that healthcare requires. Tableau remains popular for its interactive visual dashboards and intuitive drag-and-drop dashboard creation. Pricing starts at $70 per user per month, positioning it in the premium tier. Organizations choose Tableau when visualization quality and analytical flexibility matter more than cost. Looker Studio is listed among the best healthcare business intelligence software for its robust analytics capabilities and Google ecosystem integration. The platform works particularly well for organizations already using Google Workspace and Google Cloud Platform. Sisense is recognized as a top tool in healthcare BI, providing strong data integration and advanced analytics functionality. The platform excels at embedded analytics, allowing healthcare software vendors to incorporate BI directly into their applications. Domo is recommended for its user-friendly interface and real-time data insights. The platform emphasizes ease of use and collaboration, making it popular with organizations that prioritize broad user adoption over advanced analytical capabilities. Basedash stands out as an AI-native business intelligence platform built specifically for modern healthcare teams that need to move fast. Unlike traditional BI tools that require weeks of setup and dashboard configuration, Basedash lets you start asking questions of your healthcare data immediately using natural language. The platform is HIPAA compliant out of the box, which means you can connect your patient databases, claims systems, and operational data without worrying about compliance violations. What makes Basedash particularly valuable for healthcare organizations is how it handles the complexity of healthcare data without making you become a SQL expert. You can ask questions like “which patients are at highest risk for readmission this month” or “show me average length of stay by diagnosis code” and get answers instantly. The AI agent doesn’t just query your database. It generates visualizations, identifies patterns, and can even take action on your data when needed. For healthcare teams dealing with multiple data sources, Basedash eliminates the typical integration headaches. Connect your EHR, billing system, lab results, and any other databases you use. The platform handles the joins and relationships automatically. This means your clinical team, operations staff, and finance department can all work from the same data foundation without waiting for the IT team to build custom integrations. The real advantage shows up in speed to insight. Traditional BI implementations take months and require dedicated analysts to maintain dashboards. Basedash gets you up and running in days, and non-technical users can explore data independently. When a medical director wants to understand patient flow patterns or a CFO needs to analyze revenue cycle metrics, they don’t submit tickets. They just ask. Get a demo to see how Basedash can transform your healthcare data into actionable insights while maintaining full HIPAA compliance. Specialized AI-native healthcare analytics and imaging platforms Amazon Comprehend Medical provides pre-trained AI models specifically designed to extract medical concepts and insights from textual healthcare data. The service identifies medications, diagnoses, treatments, and patient demographics from unstructured text without requiring custom model training. AI-driven healthcare analytics significantly improve medical imaging by enabling sharper, faster diagnostics. Radiologists working with AI assistance can review more cases with higher accuracy, addressing the global shortage of radiologists while improving patient care. Arcadia’s data platform integrates AI-driven insights directly into clinical systems that clinicians use daily. This embedded approach ensures insights influence care decisions rather than sitting unused in separate reporting systems. The platform transforms healthcare data into actionable intelligence that improves care quality. Healthcare AI tools are transforming the industry by enhancing resource efficiency. Predictions indicate AI can automate up to 15% of healthcare work hours, creating capacity equivalent to hiring thousands of additional staff without the associated costs and recruitment challenges. AI platforms offer major benefits by reducing diagnostic errors up to 30% and streamlining operations through efficient data analysis. These accuracy improvements directly translate to better patient outcomes and reduced malpractice risk. Cloud provider healthcare AI and BI ecosystems Power BI offers deep integration with healthcare IT ecosystems, particularly for organizations using Azure, Dynamics 365, and Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare. This tight integration means data flows smoothly between systems without complex custom development. Cloud-based BI solutions are favored for their scalability, ease of maintenance, and cost-efficiency among hospitals and clinics of all sizes. The cloud model eliminates infrastructure management overhead, allowing IT teams to focus on leveraging insights rather than maintaining servers. Integration with EHR systems makes seamless data aggregation possible in cloud-based BI workflows. Modern cloud platforms connect to on-premises EHR systems through secure gateways, enabling hybrid architectures that meet security requirements while providing cloud scalability. Providers use cloud-based BI tools to support clinical, financial, and administrative decisions aimed at improving patient outcomes and operational efficiency. The accessibility of cloud platforms means stakeholders can access insights from anywhere, enabling faster decision-making. Microsoft’s Power BI is known for its scalability and affordability, with self-service capabilities that allow business users to build reports with minimal technical expertise. This democratization of analytics helps healthcare organizations develop data literacy across all roles. Essential considerations for choosing the best healthcare AI BI tool Selecting the right healthcare BI platform requires evaluating multiple factors beyond just features and pricing. The decision impacts workflows, adoption rates, and ultimately whether you’ll achieve the promised benefits. Many organizations rush this decision and regret it later. Cloud-based BI solutions are increasingly favored in healthcare for their scalability, ease of maintenance, and cost efficiency. Small practices can access capabilities that previously required enterprise budgets. Large health systems can scale across hundreds of facilities without linear infrastructure growth. Real-time dashboards and interactive visualization in healthcare BI tools allow managers to monitor key performance indicators and respond quickly to emerging issues. Static reports that arrive hours or days after events happen don’t enable the rapid response that modern healthcare demands. Integration with EHR systems enhances seamless data aggregation and improves data-driven decision-making. Poor integration creates data quality issues, delays, and user frustration. The best BI platforms feel like natural extensions of existing clinical systems rather than separate tools. Healthcare BI tools should support fine-grained access control, advanced permissions, and dynamic data masking to meet security and compliance requirements. Not everyone should see all data. Proper access controls ensure staff see only what they need for their roles. Healthcare providers increasingly prioritize data-driven decision-making through BI tools to enhance clinical, financial, and administrative outcomes. The organizations leading in quality and efficiency are the ones that have successfully embedded analytics into daily workflows rather than treating it as a separate reporting function. HIPAA compliance and data security: A non-negotiable requirement Healthcare BI systems must handle HIPAA seamlessly alongside other compliance requirements like GDPR. Patient data protection isn’t optional or negotiable. Platforms need robust encryption for data at rest and in transit, comprehensive access controls, and detailed audit trails that track who accessed what data when. Data encryption is critical for maintaining HIPAA compliance. Tools like Power BI use Azure’s encryption services for data at rest and ensure secure communication for data in transit. These technical controls are foundational, not optional extras. Meeting healthcare BI software compliance involves implementing strict data governance policies, including strong user access controls and audit trails. Organizations face substantial legal and financial risks from breaches or compliance violations. The right BI platform reduces this risk through built-in security features. Healthcare BI tools must facilitate de-identified reporting to support research while protecting patient identities. Researchers need access to data for population health studies and outcomes research. Proper de-identification allows this while protecting individual privacy. For effective HIPAA compliance, healthcare BI tools typically feature built-in security protocols to handle protected health information without compromising patient privacy or data integrity. The platform should make compliance easier, not harder, with automated checks and controls that prevent common violations. Data integration and interoperability capabilities Healthcare BI tools must support seamless interoperability with standards like HL7 or FHIR to enable efficient data exchange across clinical and administrative systems. These standards ensure data moves between systems without losing meaning or context. Integration with existing systems like EHRs, billing platforms, and lab systems is crucial for effective operation of healthcare BI software. Organizations use dozens of specialized systems. BI platforms that can’t connect to key sources create blind spots in analysis. A sophisticated healthcare BI platform can consolidate siloed data from over 100 digital healthcare systems into a single platform. This consolidation creates comprehensive views of healthcare operations that wouldn’t be possible when data remains scattered across disconnected systems. Robust integration capabilities allow healthcare BI tools to connect disparate data across various departments and facilities, fostering a coherent and unified data management approach. Finance, clinical operations, and quality departments can finally work from the same data foundation. Successful data integration in healthcare BI tools is crucial for ensuring compliance with regulations like HIPAA, GDPR, and HiTrust. Integration done poorly creates security vulnerabilities. Integration done right enhances both data utility and governance. Data governance and data quality Healthcare data governance requires robust compliance with regulations like HIPAA, GDPR, BAA, SOC2, HiTrust, and CFR Part 11. Governance frameworks must integrate strict user access controls, audit trails, and encryption to meet these varied requirements simultaneously. Establishing data quality practices ensures accuracy, consistency, and trust in analytics. Poor data quality undermines even the most sophisticated analysis. Organizations must invest in validation, cleansing, and monitoring to maintain data quality over time. Assigning data ownership and appointing stewards for key datasets are crucial components in maintaining data quality and governance. Someone needs to be accountable for each major data domain. Without clear ownership, quality inevitably degrades. Automated data validation processes are essential for detecting and correcting errors. Manual validation doesn’t scale and catches only obvious problems. Automated systems can enforce business rules, check for anomalies, and flag issues in real-time. A data governance framework must enforce consistency across departments before analytics can create value. When different departments use conflicting definitions or calculate metrics differently, analysis becomes meaningless. Governance establishes and enforces the standards that make analytics reliable. Scalability, performance, and cloud deployment Healthcare BI tools must effectively manage fast-growing data volumes without performance degradation. Patient data accumulates continuously. Imaging files are enormous. Transaction volumes increase as organizations grow. Platforms that struggle with scale become bottlenecks. Cloud-based BI solutions are increasingly adopted in healthcare for their scalability and cost-efficiency advantages. Organizations pay for what they use and scale seamlessly as needs change. This flexibility is particularly valuable for growing healthcare systems. Scalability in BI tools allows for flexible data access, which is crucial for hospitals and clinics managing large and complex datasets. During crises or surges, demand for analytics spikes dramatically. Platforms need to handle these peaks without slowing down. Cloud and hybrid deployment models are popular for healthcare systems needing scalable and secure AI platforms. Pure cloud works for many organizations. Others require hybrid models that keep sensitive data on-premises while using cloud compute for analysis. Good platforms support both. Cloud-based BI tools offer ease of maintenance, which contributes to operational efficiency. Updates and patches happen automatically without downtime. Security improvements deploy immediately. Organizations avoid the complexity of managing on-premises infrastructure. User-friendliness and self-service analytics Power BI provides a cost-effective, user-friendly analytics experience, especially for healthcare organizations needing to analyze and visualize data. The familiar Excel-like interface reduces the learning curve. Users comfortable with spreadsheets can quickly become proficient with Power BI. Integration capabilities with familiar platforms like Microsoft Excel enhance the user-friendliness of Power BI for organizations already using Microsoft services. Users can start in Excel and publish to Power BI, or pull Power BI insights into Excel. This flexibility meets users where they already work. Advanced healthcare BI tools feature real-time dashboards and interactive visualization that contribute to more accessible and comprehensive data analysis. The best visualizations communicate insights instantly without requiring explanation. Good design makes complexity understandable. Modern healthcare BI tools enable the consolidation of data from disparate systems through user-friendly interfaces that allow for holistic business views. Users don’t need to understand database schemas or table relationships. The platform handles the complexity behind intuitive interfaces. Self-service capabilities determine whether BI tools get used by a small analytics team or adopted broadly across the organization. When anyone can ask questions and get answers, insights spread faster and influence more decisions. Total cost of ownership and return on investment Understanding the full cost of healthcare BI platforms requires looking beyond license fees. Implementation costs, training time, ongoing maintenance, data integration work, and the opportunity cost of delayed insights all contribute to total cost of ownership. Organizations report achieving 6x ROI with automated data governance by reducing manual compliance work and avoiding penalties. The time savings alone often justify the investment before considering the value of better insights. Getting up to 368% ROI through HIPAA-compliant healthcare BI practices is achievable when you factor in improved operational efficiency, reduced readmissions, and better resource utilization. The ROI calculation should include both cost savings and revenue improvements. License costs are just the starting point. Power BI starts at $10 per user monthly but requires Azure infrastructure and potentially Premium capacity for enterprise features. Tableau starts at $70 per user monthly with different licensing models for creators versus viewers. Understanding the full cost structure prevents budget surprises. The value of better insights often exceeds the cost of platforms. Reducing readmissions by even 1% through predictive analytics can save millions annually for large health systems. Optimizing staffing can reduce overtime costs substantially. These benefits typically dwarf platform costs when measured honestly. title: Settle Your QA Debt Before the Bugs Start Breaking Kneecaps
summary: Practical strategies to eliminate QA bottlenecks and build resilient testing pipelines
body_text: Introduction In Part One , we discussed how QA debt builds silently over time — causing slower releases, late-night firefights, and unpredictable test cycles. The next step is understanding how much debt you have and where it hides. This post goes deeper into measuring QA debt — what to track, how to collect data, and how to use those insights to create a sustainable plan for improvement. 1. Quantify Your QA Debt with Actionable Metrics QA debt is invisible until you attach real numbers to it. Below are six measurable indicators — each with its definition , collection method , and what it reveals about your testing maturity. A. Test Coverage Definition: The percentage of your code, APIs, or user journeys covered by automated tests. How to Collect: Use your CI pipeline or test framework (e.g., Jest, Pytest, JUnit, Cypress) to generate coverage reports. Analyze at the service level , not just line coverage — for example, what percentage of API endpoints have automated test cases? Key Insight: Low coverage in critical paths (login, checkout, API gateways) often hides latent bugs and slows your release cycle. Benchmark: 70–80% coverage for core services 100% coverage for authentication and payment logic Debt Indicator: If manual QA is still required for high-traffic or revenue-impacting paths, coverage debt exists. B. Automation Ratio Definition: The ratio of automated tests to total tests in your regression or release cycle. How to Collect: Track the total number of automated tests in your CI/CD logs. Compare against the total number of manual test cases in your QA management tool (like TestRail or Zephyr). Formula (automation rate): Automation Ratio=Automated TestsTotal Tests×100\text{Automation Ratio} = \frac{\text{Automated Tests}}{\text{Total Tests}} \times 100 Automation Ratio = Total Tests Automated Tests ​ × 100 Key Insight: A low automation ratio means every release depends on manual validation — slowing releases and increasing human error. Benchmark: 85% for regression; manual testing should focus on exploratory validation only. Debt Indicator: If manual testing consumes more than 30% of QA time per sprint, automation debt is significant. C. Defect Leakage Rate Definition: The percentage of bugs that escape into production versus those caught in testing. How to Collect: Pull defect data from Jira or your bug tracker. Categorize bugs by where they were detected (QA vs. production). Formula (leaks): Defect Leakage=Prod BugsTotal Bugs×100\text{Defect Leakage} = \frac{\text{Prod Bugs}}{\text{Total Bugs}} \times 100 Defect Leakage = Total Bugs Prod Bugs ​ × 100 Key Insight: This is the most direct measure of QA effectiveness. A rising leakage trend means QA debt is growing faster than it’s being paid down. Benchmark: <10% defect leakage is healthy; >20% suggests broken test coverage or unstable environments. Debt Indicator: If production issues are frequently linked to missed test scenarios, your QA suite isn’t keeping up with real-world usage — a prime use case for traffic replay testing with tools like Speedscale. D. Flaky Test Rate Definition: The percentage of tests that fail intermittently without code changes. How to Collect: Use your CI/CD logs to track test results over time. Identify tests that pass and fail inconsistently across identical builds. Formula (flake rate): Flaky Test Rate=Flaky TestsTotal Tests×100\text{Flaky Test Rate} = \frac{\text{Flaky Tests}}{\text{Total Tests}} \times 100 Flaky Test Rate = Total Tests Flaky Tests ​ × 100 Key Insight: Flaky tests erode developer confidence — they cause false negatives, wasted debugging time, and often get ignored or skipped. Benchmark: <5% is acceptable. Debt Indicator: If developers regularly disable tests or rerun pipelines to “make them pass,” you have technical QA debt tied to instability. E. Environment Parity Score Definition: How closely your test environments match production in configuration, data, and dependencies. How to Collect: Create a checklist comparing staging vs. production: API versions, config flags, database schemas, message queues, third-party mocks. Score each category from 1 (not aligned) to 5 (identical). Formula (average): Environment Parity Score=Sum of Category ScoresTotal Categories\text{Environment Parity Score} = \frac{\text{Sum of Category Scores}}{\text{Total Categories}} Environment Parity Score = Total Categories Sum of Category Scores ​ Key Insight: The closer your test environment is to production, the more predictive your QA results are. Benchmark: ≥4 out of 5 indicates high fidelity. Debt Indicator: If certain systems (like payments or legacy services) are only testable in production, environment debt is high — this is where ephemeral environments or virtualized APIs can make a huge impact. F. Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Resolve (MTTR) Definition: How long it takes to discover and fix issues once they’re introduced. How to Collect: Use your CI/CD and observability tools (Datadog, Grafana, Sentry, etc.) to timestamp when failures are detected vs. when fixes are deployed. Formulas (responsiveness): Calulating Mean Time to Detection (MTTD): MTTD=Total Detection TimeNumber of Incidents\text{MTTD} = \frac{\text{Total Detection Time}}{\text{Number of Incidents}} MTTD = Number of Incidents Total Detection Time ​ Calculating Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR): MTTR=Total Resolution TimeNumber of Incidents\text{MTTR} = \frac{\text{Total Resolution Time}}{\text{Number of Incidents}} MTTR = Number of Incidents Total Resolution Time ​ Key Insight: High MTTD/MTTR values indicate that QA lacks fast feedback loops. Benchmark: MTTD: <30 minutes in CI/CD MTTR: <1 business day for high-priority defects Debt Indicator: Slow feedback cycles suggest reactive QA rather than proactive prevention — a hallmark of deep QA debt. 2. Using Metrics to Create a QA Debt Index Once collected, combine these metrics into a QA Debt Index (QDI) — a simple weighted score that gives you an at-a-glance measure of your overall quality posture. Metric Weight Ideal Risk Threshold Test Coverage 20% >80% <60% Automation Ratio 15% >85% <60% Defect Leakage 25% <10% >20% Flaky Test Rate 10% <5% >15% Environment Parity 15% ≥4/5 ≤3/5 MTTD/MTTR 15% Fast (<1 day) Slow (>3 days) Each quarter, calculate your QDI and track whether QA improvements are reducing risk or just moving the debt around. 3. Why “Move Fast and Break Things” Doesn’t Work for Mature Applications Early-stage startups can afford to prioritize agility over stability. Shipping quickly — even if it means introducing bugs — is acceptable when users are few, data is simple, and downtime has minimal impact. But as systems scale and products mature, the cost of breaking things skyrockets . At that point, the strategy must evolve from “release fast” to “release fast with confidence.” Here’s why: Customer Impact: Mature applications serve paying customers who expect reliability. Every regression or outage erodes trust and brand equity. Complex Systems: Modern architectures (microservices, event-driven APIs, global deployments) multiply the blast radius of even minor bugs. Compliance and Risk: In regulated industries — finance, healthcare, or enterprise SaaS — quality failures can mean real financial or legal penalties. Velocity Paradox: Teams that chase speed without stability eventually slow down. Uncontrolled QA debt leads to brittle releases, firefighting, and fewer deployable builds over time. And beyond the technical risk, there’s a real human cost . We’ve seen VPs of Engineering and senior leaders lose their jobs after releasing code that wasn’t fully tested — even when the intent was to accelerate delivery. Leadership carries the accountability for reliability, and when systems fail, the spotlight lands at the top. Mature engineering organizations don’t just move fast — they move deliberately. They rely on automation, replay-based testing, and continuous quality metrics to keep velocity and reliability aligned. Speed without confidence isn’t agility — it’s volatility. Sustainable agility comes from repeatable, automated, and observable QA processes that scale with your system’s complexity. By tracking trends in test coverage, defect leakage, and environment parity, teams can see when “move fast” is turning into “move recklessly” — and correct course before it impacts production or careers. 4. How Mocking Services Enables Faster, Smarter Testing One of the most effective ways to accelerate QA without cutting corners is through service mocking — simulating the behavior of external APIs and dependencies so you can test in isolation. In complex distributed systems, real integrations are often slow, flaky, or unavailable in lower environments. Mocking eliminates that bottleneck by letting teams: Run More Tests in Parallel: Without waiting on external services, CI/CD pipelines can execute thousands of tests simultaneously. Test Edge Cases Reliably: Mocks allow you to simulate unusual responses, timeouts, and downstream failures — scenarios that are nearly impossible to reproduce in production. Reduce Environment Drift: Mocked services behave the same way every time, ensuring consistent results across dev, QA, and staging environments. Shorten Feedback Loops: Engineers can validate changes in seconds rather than hours, enabling faster iteration without sacrificing quality. The result? Higher test coverage, shorter release cycles, and fewer production surprises. By integrating mocking into your test strategy — especially when paired with traffic replay tools like Speedscale — you get realistic behavior without the fragility of live dependencies. It’s the foundation of testing at scale with confidence. 5. Make QA Debt Reduction Sustainable Allocate a fixed percentage of each sprint to reducing QA debt — similar to refactoring code. For example: Week 1: Identify flaky tests Week 2: Stabilize test environments Week 3: Automate missing regression paths Week 4: Review metrics and update the QDI Consistent investment compounds over time — turning QA debt into QA capital. Conclusion The “move fast and break things” era ends when your users, systems, and responsibilities grow. Mature applications demand disciplined agility — the ability to move quickly because you trust your tests, not in spite of them. By measuring QA metrics, tracking trends, using mocks for repeatable testing, and rejecting the idea that speed justifies instability, teams can build software that’s both fast and reliable. QA debt isn’t just a technical burden — it’s a business and leadership risk. Managing it effectively gives you what every engineering leader wants: the confidence to ship at any speed.

title: Can I ( A no-coder) use Puppeteer to submit a form
summary: I can automate data entry and form submission without writing a single line of code. I'm a no-code automation expert. I build workflows without touching JavaScript.
body_text: I can automate data entry and form submission without writing a single line of code. I'm a no-code automation expert. I build workflows without touching JavaScript. This week, it’s time to shake things up. Axiom has just released a new tool that lets you run multiple Puppeteer scripts concurrently in Chrome browsers directly from the command line. Now's the perfect time to level up and learn some Puppeteer. Following on from coding a simple web scraper , I'm now going to automate a web form with code. If you’re a Puppeteer expert, give our new tool a spin. Why I’m not saying “use AI” when everyone else is hyping it: LLMs just aren’t suited to this. They’re costly, error-prone, and bad for the planet. Code or no-code is faster and cleaner. Use LLMs to learn, but not for repetitive tasks. If you’re learning like me, Hi I’m Alex Barlow, co-founder of Axiom. Let’s dive in. How do I automate forms without code? I first select the source of my data, usually a Google Sheet or webhook. I look at the web form, then add the necessary steps in the No-code tool to create my workflow. Before I can test the bot, I need to select the elements and connect the data, and I'm done. My no-code experience will be useful here. I’m betting that many of the same steps we have in Axiom map directly to methods in Puppeteer. Why Puppeeter and not Playwright? We’ve built a tool that runs code remotely in Chrome browsers using CDP a WebSocket-based API that enables programmatic interaction with Chrome and Chromium-based browsers, and I want to learn how to use it. I have extensive knowledge of browser automation, but I'm not familiar with coding bots. If I am to work with the team in developing the tool, I need to learn. The new tool can also run Playwright, but I am choosing Puppeteer becuase our no-code tool extends it. Tools I will use, including an AI I will be using an AI, probably ChatGPT or Claude, to help me learn how to script Puppeteer automations. AI is a great learning tool and helps me avoid bugging our CTO with stupid questions. I will also be using Cusor to script and run my automation. Finally, I will be running the script with Axiom's new endpoint for browser automation. Get setting up with Axiom An Axiom account is required to run code in our cloud. It's free to try; all new accounts get 30 minutes of runtime. No credit card required. We do not share user information with third parties or send marketing emails. This example code shows you how to connect to the service and open a window. I will use it as a starting point for coding my bot. const browser = await puppeteer. connect ({ /// Insert my axiom API Key here browserWSEndpoint: " Insert Api key" }); const page = await browser. newPage () /// Set window size await page. setViewport ({ width: 1960 , height: 1080 }); /// Insert URL of webform I wish to automate await page. goto ( "URl" ) await page. close () await browser. close () What puppeteer commands should I use? Off the bat, I could be lazy and ask an LLM to write the code for me. But I want to learn. So instead, I’m using generative AI to research Puppeteer commands. The first thing I learned was about Puppeteer's Page class and the methods it provides for interacting with an open browser tab, such as navigating to URLs, clicking elements, typing text, and taking screenshots — all the good stuff we browser automators like. What does "await" mean? In the course of my research, I learned that Puppeteer’s methods are asynchronous. That means they start an action and move on without waiting for it to finish. When we interact with a web page, we do things synchronously — we click, wait, then move to the next step. So imagine the chaos if a script tried to fill in every form field at once! I found that these asynchronous methods return a promise — “I’ll let you know when this is done.” The await tells JavaScript to wait for that promise before running the next line. It stops the script from firing off everything in one mad rush, making the automation more human-like. How to input text into a field using puppeteer To enter text into a field, I use the type method. This method works like saying: “On this page (the current tab), type this text into the element that matches this selector.” For example: // Types text into an input await page. type ( '#username' , 'myUser' ); I also learnt you can use another method fill which is faster but type is more human as it simulates key strokes. How to automate a sleect list using puppeteer To chose an option from a select list, I use the select method. This method works like saying: “On this page (the current tab), select X on the element that matches this selector.” For example: // Select an option by its value attribute await page. select ( '#mySelect' , 'optionValue' ); optionValue is th evalue you want to select. How to click an element using puppeteer To click an element like a link, I use the click method. This method works like saying: “On this page (the current tab), select and click element that matches this selector.” For example: await page. click ( '#loginButton' ); You could also try co-ordinates, see example: await page. click ( '#loginButton' , { offset: { x: 10 , y: 5 } }); How to select radio button using puppeteer To click a radio, I use the click method again. This method works like saying: “On this page (the current tab), select and click radio that matches this selector.” For example: await page. click ( 'input[type=radio][value=cat]' ); Last but not least, How to use a keypress to automate website actions To replicate keyboard actions, I can use the keypress method. This method works like saying: “On this page (the current tab), press this key.” For example: await page.keyboard. press ( 'Enter' ); Typically, I use the no-code keypress step in Axiom to submit forms or tab between elements. I can, of course, do the same with code. Coding the bot First up, I’ll insert my API key and the URL of the web form I’ll automate, in this case a demo page. const browser = await puppeteer. connect ({ /// Insert my axiom API Key here browserWSEndpoint: "eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxOTUzNzMsInRva2VuIjoiMTk1MzczNDZhMTA4OWIwYmQzZWRmNyJ9" }); const page = await browser. newPage () await page. setViewport ({ width: 1960 , height: 1080 }); /// Insert URL of webform I wish to automate await page. goto ( "https://axiom.ai/demo/webform/" ) await page. close () await browser. close () Selecting Puppeteer methods to automate the form Now into uncharted water I have done this without code using Axiom, just never with code. Looking at the form I see I will need: The type method to submit name and email The Select method to select an option on "How did you find us" select list A click method to select a radio Finally, A click method to click submit I add five lines of code. For each one, I also need a CSS selector . To work out my selectors, I use Chrome Inspector, a tool I’m familiar with and use a lot when building no-code automations. const browser = await puppeteer. connect ({ /// Insert my axiom API Key here browserWSEndpoint: "eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxOTUzNzMsInRva2VuIjoiMTk1MzczNDZhMTA4OWIwYmQzZWRmNyJ9" }); const page = await browser. newPage () /// Set window size await page. setViewport ({ width: 1960 , height: 1080 }); /// Insert URL of webform I wish to automate await page. goto ( "https://axiom.ai/demo/webform/" ) // Enter name added css selector await page. type ( '#name' , 'myUser' ); // Enter email added css selector await page. type ( '#email' , 'myUser' ); // Select list added css selector and value await page. select ( '#howFound' , 'Referral' ); // Radio added css selector await page. click ( '#optInYes' ); // Submit form added css selector await page. click ( '.submit-btn' ); await page. close () await browser. close () Testing and running the Puppeteer script There are two ways to test my bot. Run the script from console or in cursor by simply entering node form-entry-bot.js . Alternaticaley I can run the script inside the tools "Live editor" feature which is found in the code dashboard web app . Each method has pros and cons. From the command line, you can’t watch the run, but you do get feedback on the run state, errors, and other details. In the Live editor, a preview opens so you can watch the run — as shown in the screenshot below. Minnor tweak to the code I tested the script in the desktop Live editor. The click on the submit button wasn’t visible on the page, so I added a line of code to scroll. The page also closed too quickly, so I added a wait to keep it open. Other than that, it worked perfectly. await page. evaluate (() => { document. querySelector ( '.submit-btn' ). scrollIntoView (); }); // Submit form await page. click ( '.submit-btn' ); // Wait to see the result await new Promise ( resolve => setTimeout (resolve, 5000 )); Wrapping up — yes, a no-coder can learn Puppeteer and automate a form, but should you? I've been using Puppeteer for years without really understanding much about the underlying code through Axiom's no-code tool . One customer even said it's 85% faster than writing your own Puppeteer script. I've really enjoyed digging deeper into code, even though I've only scratched the surface. It's been good to learn about the page class and methods such as click . The process I went through, using AI for help, working in a tool like Cursor, and having an endpoint to test my scripts, made it easy to get up and running. No wrestling with NPM, which can be a real pain. I also learned about await , and that the page methods in Puppeteer return a promise when they are completed. As a no-coder, I can now automate forms with or without using Puppeteer. So which would I choose? I’ll be honest, I’d choose lazy every time. It's just quicker and easier to use the No-code tool. Even if I were a proficient coder, I'd still pick no-code. That said, I've really enjoyed learning more about how Puppeteer works, so I'll keep digging deeper and trying new things.
